title: How must Portuguese employers organize occupational safety and health services?
description: Portugal's Law 102/2009 on internal, common and external OSH services, the 400 and 30 worker thresholds, technician ratios, titles and 30 hour CPD rule.
shortAnswer: Portugal's Law 102/2009 requires every employer to organize an occupational safety and health service as an internal, common, or external service. An internal service is mandatory for establishments with at least 400 workers, or 30 workers exposed to high-risk activities, unless the labor authority grants an exemption. Safety work must be done by certified safety technicians in minimum numbers per workforce, and under Law 42/2012 technicians must complete 30 hours of continuous training every five years to keep their title.
keyTakeaways: Article 73 of Law 102/2009 requires every employer to organize an OSH service; failing to do so is a very serious offense.
Article 78(3) makes an internal service mandatory at 400 workers per establishment or group of establishments within 50 km, or 30 workers exposed to high-risk activities.

Article 101 sets minimum safety technician staffing: one technician up to 50 workers, and above 50, two technicians per 1,500 workers in industry or per 3,000 elsewhere, at least one a senior technician.
External OSH services need authorization from the labor authority (safety) or health authority (health), and using an unauthorized provider is a very serious offense for both parties (Article 84).
Law 42/2012 requires a professional title for safety technicians and suspends it if the holder does not complete 30 hours of continuous training in each five year period.
regulator: Autoridade para as Condições do Trabalho (ACT) for safety; Direção-Geral da Saúde (DGS) for occupational health
appliesTo: All employers in Portugal subject to Law 102/2009, including public employers through Law 79/2019
Establishments with 400 or more workers, or 30 or more workers exposed to high-risk activities
External OSH service providers seeking authorization
Senior safety technicians (técnico superior de segurança no trabalho) and safety technicians (técnico de segurança no trabalho)

sections.heading: What does Law 102/2009 require about OSH services?

blocks.text: Chapter IX of Law 102/2009 of September 10, 2009 (regime jurídico da promoção da segurança e saúde no trabalho) requires the employer to organize a safety and health service in one of the modalities the law allows. Article 73(1) states the duty and Article 73(2) makes breach a very serious offense. This page cites the full text as republished by [Law 3/2014](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2014/01/01900/0055400591.pdf) of January 28, 2014. Worker training and information duties under the same law are covered separately in [Portugal's OHS training requirements](/regulations/portugal-ohs-training-requirements).

Article 73-A sets the service's objectives, including informing and training workers on safety and health. Article 73-B lists its main activities, among them risk assessment, the prevention plan, the internal emergency plan, health surveillance, and, in points (l) and (m), designing and developing the information program and the training program for safety and health at work. Article 73-B(5) requires the employer to keep the documentation of these activities available to inspectors for five years.

Later amendments listed in the Diário da República (Decree-Law 88/2015, Law 146/2015, Law 28/2016, Law 79/2019, and Decree-Law 20/2020) changed other articles; [Law 146/2015](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2015/09/17600/0732507342.pdf), for example, amended Article 77 for ships under the Maritime Labour Convention. As at November 2026, the Chapter IX provisions cited on this page read as republished in 2014.

sections.heading: What are the internal, common, and external service modalities?

blocks.text: Article 74(1) allows three modalities: internal service, common service, and external service. Article 74(2) makes the internal service the default, with common or external services, or qualified technicians, allowed only where the company lacks sufficient internal means or where Article 81 applies. Article 74(3) and (4) allow different modalities per establishment and separate organization of safety and of health.

blocks.text: Article 74(6) states that using a common or external service does not relieve the employer of its own legal responsibility for safety and health. Article 75 requires every company, whatever the modality, to have an internal structure for emergencies, first aid, evacuation, and firefighting; breach is a very serious offense.

sections.heading: When is an internal service mandatory, and can an employer be exempted?

blocks.text: An internal service is mandatory at the thresholds in Article 78(3), unless an exemption is granted under Article 80. The thresholds are an establishment with at least 400 workers; a group of establishments within 50 km of the largest that together have at least 400 workers; or an establishment or group of establishments carrying out high-risk activities to which at least 30 workers are exposed. Article 79 lists the high-risk activities, such as construction with risk of falls or burial, extractive industries, explosives, medium and high voltage electricity, ionizing radiation, carcinogens, and silica.

Article 80(1) lets the competent authority exempt an establishment covered only by the 400 worker test if it has no high-risk activities, accident incidence and severity rates over the last two years no higher than the sector average, no record of occupational diseases linked to the company, no very serious OSH offenses in the same establishment in the last two years, and exposure limits respected. The request must include the reasoned opinion of workers' safety representatives. Under Article 80(7), if an exemption is revoked, for example after a fatal accident attributable to the employer, the company must set up an internal service within six months.

sections.heading: How many safety technicians and occupational health staff are required?

blocks.text: Article 100(1) requires safety activities to be carried out by senior safety technicians or safety technicians certified by the labor authority, who act with technical autonomy. Article 101(2) sets the minimum allocation per company:

items: Industrial establishments: up to 50 workers, one technician; above 50, two technicians for every 1,500 workers covered or fraction, at least one of them a senior technician.
Other establishments: up to 50 workers, one technician; above 50, two technicians for every 3,000 workers covered or fraction, at least one of them a senior technician.

blocks.text: Article 101(3) allows the labor authority to require more time where the nature or severity of risks or accident indicators justify it, and breach is a serious offense. On the health side, Article 104(1) requires the occupational physician to be assisted by a nurse in companies with more than 250 workers, and Article 105(2) sets minimum physician presence: at least one hour per month per 10 workers in industrial or high-risk establishments, and one hour per month per 20 workers elsewhere. Article 105(3) caps a physician at 150 hours of activity per month.

For external providers, Article 85(1)(a) requires the permanent availability of at least one senior technician and one safety technician, and of an occupational physician, as a condition of authorization.

sections.heading: What qualifications and continuous training do safety technicians need?

blocks.text: [Law 42/2012](https://files.diariodarepublica.pt/1s/2012/08/16600/0476104766.pdf) of August 28, 2012 sets the rules for access to and exercise of the professions of senior safety technician and safety technician. Article 3(1) allows the professions to be exercised only by holders of a valid professional title, and Article 3(2) makes a contract to work without one void. Hiring a technician without a title is a serious offense for the employer under Article 3(5).

blocks.text: Article 8(1) states that the certifying entity suspends the title where, in each five year period, the technician has not completed at least 30 hours of continuous training, or 100 hours if they have practiced for less than two years. The suspension ends once the training is proved. Article 7(1)(c) also lists acquiring and updating competences among the profession's ethical duties. Under Article 20, certificates of professional aptitude issued under the previous law count as professional titles.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each OSH service obligation with its trigger, such as a headcount threshold or a title renewal period, and links technician CPD to the competences in the professional profile. That lets an employer show which service model applies, who delivers it, and whether each technician's title is current, from one set of records. The same structure supports [energy and resources](/industries/energy-resources) operators with high-risk activities.

faqs.q: Can a company with 500 office workers use an external OSH service?
faqs.a: Only with an exemption. At 400 workers per establishment Article 78(3) requires an internal service, but Article 80 lets the labor or health authority grant an exemption where there are no high-risk activities, accident rates are not above the sector average, and the other conditions are met. Without an exemption, failing to set up an internal service is a very serious offense.

faqs.q: Does a safety technician's title expire in Portugal?
faqs.a: It does not expire on a fixed date, but under Article 8 of Law 42/2012 it is suspended if the holder does not complete at least 30 hours of continuous training in each five year period, or 100 hours if they have practiced for less than two years. The suspension ends once the training is proved.

Under Article 84(3) of Law 102/2009, the labor authority's OSH body authorizes services in the safety domain and the health ministry's competent body authorizes services in the health domain. Authorization can cover one or both areas and specific sectors or high-risk activities.

faqs.q: How is this page different from Portugal's OHS training page?
faqs.a: This page covers how the OSH service itself must be organized, staffed, and qualified. Worker training and information duties, consultation on the training program, and training for first aid and emergency staff are covered on the Portugal OHS training requirements page.
